hero.lede: Avo runs Android apps and games on your Mac. Each one opens in its own window, with its own Dock icon and a place in ⌘Tab.
hero.hubLink: Meet Avo Hub, for your phone
hero.factMac: Any Mac with M1 or newer
hero.factPrivate: No account, no ads, no tracking
hero.libraryCaption: Pick up where you left off, or open any app.
hero.libraryAlt: Avo's library window on a Mac: Garena Delta Force to continue playing, then rows of Android games and apps such as Call of Duty, Google Play, Chrome and Settings.
hero.playCaption: A shooter in its own window, keys over its touch controls.
hero.playAlt: A shooter in its own Mac window, with round labels for W, A, S, D, Q, E, Space and the mouse buttons placed over the game's touch controls, and 59 FPS in the top corner. Player names are blurred.
hero.keysCaption: Drag a key onto a button, then press the key you want.
hero.keysAlt: Avo's key editor over a game's lobby: a toolbar with Add Control and Templates, and key labels such as W, A, S, D, Q, E and the mouse buttons on the game's buttons.
hero.settingsCaption: Frame rate, render scale and sharpness, per app.
hero.settingsAlt: Avo's Graphics settings: the renderer uses the Mac's graphics chip, the frame rate cap is 60, with controls for render scale, interface size, scaling filter and sharpness.

mac.title: Your Mac's shortcuts, in every Android app.
mac.lede: Avo gives each Android app a Mac menu bar with the keys you already know. Search them the way you would in a Mac's Help menu.
mac.switchText: Every Android app has its own window and Dock icon, and shows up in Launchpad, Spotlight and ⌘Tab.
mac.switchTerms: window dock launchpad spotlight switch app
mac.gameText: Your keys and mouse press the game's touch controls. In shooters, the mouse looks around.
mac.keysText: Drag keys onto a game's buttons, or start from a layout made for shooters, MOBAs or racing games.
mac.keysTerms: keys keymap controls layout template controller
mac.translateText: The text in any app, translated in place on your Mac.
mac.shotText: Just the app's window, nothing else on your screen, saved to Pictures.
mac.recordText: The app and its sound, saved to Movies. Press the keys again to stop.
mac.locationText: Android uses your Mac's location, or a place or a route you pick on the map.
mac.perfText: Frame rate and frame time, right in the corner of the window.
mac.pasteText: One clipboard for both sides. Links in Android open in your Mac's browser.
mac.also: Notifications arrive in Notification Center, with Reply. Dark mode, time zone, 24-hour clock and language follow your Mac. Drag files in from Finder, and let the media keys and AirPods control what Android plays.
mac.notYet: Bluetooth headsets and phone calls don't work yet.

games.lede: Turn on Game Mode and each key presses the touch control under it. Pick a key to see where it lands.
games.shotPlayAlt: A shooter in its own Mac window, with round labels for W, A, S, D, Q, E, Space and the mouse buttons placed over the game's touch controls, and the frame rate in the top corner. Player names are blurred.
games.shotKeysAlt: Avo's key editor over a game's lobby: a toolbar with Add Control and Templates, and key labels such as W, A, S, D, Q, E and the mouse buttons placed on the game's buttons.
games.controller: Prefer a controller? Connect it to your Mac and play.
games.status: Games are still being tested. Avo adds no auto-aim or other advantages, and some online games refuse to run in Avo; it won't try to get around that.
games.shotNote: Player names and account numbers in these screenshots are blurred.

playMove.text: Move. The four keys push the game's on-screen stick.

playLook.text: Look around, as far as you like. One key frees the pointer and takes it back.

playFire.text: Fire, for as long as you hold the button. Avo adds no rapid fire.

playJump.text: Each key presses the button under it: Space jumps, C crouches, R reloads.

playFps.text: How smoothly the game runs, right in the corner.

keysAdd.text: Adds a new key. Drag it onto the game's button.

keysTemplates.text: Start from a ready-made layout for shooters, MOBAs or racing games.

keysKey.text: Select a key, then press the one you want. Drag to move it, use the corner to resize it, × to remove it.

keysLook.text: Where the mouse swipes to turn the camera. Drag its edges to fit the game.

keysPad.text: Four keys on one stick. A controller's d-pad can push it too.

keysMouse.text: With a key selected, right-click to pick a mouse button or the scroll wheel instead.

how.title: How Avo works
how.s1Text: A small Android system starts in the background, walled off from the rest of your Mac. You never see a phone screen, and you can change versions or go back to the one before.
how.s1Alt: Avo's Android settings: Android 17 is installed with the June 2026 security update, Android 16 is kept as the previous version, with buttons to change versions, switch back or reset Android.
how.s2Title: Your Mac's graphics chip draws it.
how.s2Text: Apple chips run Android apps directly, without slow translation. Cap games at 30, 60, 90 or 120 frames per second, or match your display.
how.s2Alt: Avo's Graphics settings: the renderer is set to Automatic and uses the Mac's graphics chip, the frame rate cap is 60, and there are controls for render scale, interface size, scaling filter and sharpness.
how.s3Title: Apps see the phone you choose.
how.s3Text: Pick the phone model apps see, and whether Android may use your Mac's location. Apps that ask for a fingerprint still work.
how.s3Alt: Avo's Privacy & Security settings: a device profile set to identify as a OnePlus 13, with its chipset, graphics and screen listed, and a switch that shares the Mac's location with Android.
how.s4Title: Google Play, if you want it.
how.s4Text: Play isn't included. Avo can add it, and helps you register with Google before you sign in. F-Droid and other stores work too.
how.s4Alt: Avo's Google Apps settings: the Play Store and Play services are installed, the Android ID is blurred, and a button copies the ID to register with Google before signing in.

req.title: What your Mac needs
req.chipText: Any Mac with an M1 chip or newer. Intel Macs aren't supported.
req.osText: macOS 15 or newer. Avo uses features that arrived with it.
req.diskText: For Android, your apps and their data. No Android Studio needed.
req.sizeText: Setup then fetches Android from Google's public AOSP build server.

hubTeaser.title: Have an Android phone too?
hubTeaser.text: Avo needs no phone. Avo Hub is for the one in your pocket: its screen, notifications, messages, calls and files on your Mac, over a cable, Wi‑Fi or the internet. It's a separate app, in development.
hubTeaser.alt: Avo Hub's window on a Mac: a Pixel 9 connected over USB at 82% battery with an Open Screen button, a reminder about battery optimisation, and recent notifications and messages.

dev.title: Open source, with adb built in.
dev.adb: Connect adb and Android Studio with one switch in Settings.
dev.root: Test on Android 17, with a root shell and a command-line tool.
dev.source: All the code is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. Build it yourself or send a pull request.

built.textNamed: Made by {maintainer} in West Kalimantan, with help from Claude.
built.textAnon: Made by an independent developer in West Kalimantan, with help from Claude.

support.title: Avo is free. Your support keeps it going.
support.text: Avo is built and maintained by one independent developer. Your support goes straight to that work: development tools, test hardware, and the Apple Developer Program fee that lets Avo open without a security warning.
support.note: Support goes to the developer personally. It is not a purchase and does not come with features or priority help.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Yes. No price, no ads and no account needed.
faq.a2: Now: use the download button, or get it from GitHub Releases. It’s notarized, so it opens like any app, and from 1.0 on it updates itself.
faq.a3: We're still testing. Some online games block programs like Avo, and Avo won't try to get around that.
faq.a4: It isn't included, but you can add it in Avo's settings. Other stores, like F-Droid, work too.
faq.a5: Usually not. Most banking apps only run on a real phone.
faq.a6: Android runs walled off from the rest of your Mac, and Avo's code is open for anyone to check.
faq.q7: Does it work on Intel Macs?
faq.a7: No. You need a Mac with an Apple chip, M1 or newer.
faq.a8: To the developer, personally. It pays for the tools and hardware Avo is built and tested with, and for the Apple Developer Program fee that lets Avo open without a security warning.

cta.title: Ready when your Mac is.
cta.text: Open the disk image, drag Avo to Applications and open it. Setup downloads Android and starts it, and from then on Avo keeps itself up to date.
cta.dmgAlt: Avo's disk image window: the Avo icon, an arrow, and the Applications folder, with the words Drag Avo into Applications.

hero.factFree: Free over a cable and the same Wi‑Fi

features.title: Your phone, from your Mac.
features.lede: Reply to a text, copy a code, take a call or find a file, from the Mac in front of you.
features.notifText: They land in Notification Center. Reply, dismiss, or copy a one-time code without touching the phone.
features.notifAlt: Avo Hub's Notifications: a WhatsApp conversation with Reply and Mark as Read, a bank's verification code, a Gmail summary, and notifications the phone keeps private.
features.messagesText: Read and send text messages from your Mac. A code in a message gets its own Copy button.
features.messagesAlt: Avo Hub's Messages: three conversations, and a bank's verification code 482913 with a Copy button.
features.callsText: See who's calling, answer or decline, or dial from the Mac's keypad. The call's sound stays on the phone.
features.callsAlt: Avo Hub's Calls: recent calls, an incoming call from Rani with Answer and Decline buttons, and a keypad.
features.filesText: Browse the phone's folders and gallery, save originals to your Mac, and send files back.
features.filesAlt: Avo Hub's Files: the Camera folder of a Pixel 9 with photo names, dates, sizes and kinds, and 112.4 GB free.
features.readyText: Phone brands add battery savers and settings that get in the way. The readiness check finds each one and shows what to do.
features.readyAlt: Avo Hub's Readiness page: 7 checks ready, 2 needing attention (battery optimization and wireless debugging) and 3 not sure yet, each with Show on Phone.
features.alsoWebcam: Your phone's camera as a webcam in any Mac app.
features.alsoDisplay: A phone or tablet as an extra display for your Mac.
features.alsoFind: Ring the phone at full volume, even on silent. Battery and signal stay in the menu bar.
features.alsoRemote: Remote Screen: your Mac's screen on the phone, your finger as the trackpad. Off until you turn it on.
features.alsoWeb: Avo Hub Web and Avo Remote Web: your phones and your Mac from any browser, with an account.
features.alsoClip: While the phone's screen is open, copy on one and paste on the other.
features.status: Avo Hub is still in development. These features are built and being tested, and may change before the first release.

how.title: How it connects
how.s1Text: Turn on USB debugging and connect the phone to your Mac with a cable. Avo Hub puts its app on the phone, and the setup assistant walks you through the rest.
how.s2Text: Scan the code on your Mac with the phone. If both screens show the same six digits, confirm on both. Phones on your account skip this.
how.s3Text: At home it goes over the cable or the same Wi‑Fi; away, over the internet, end-to-end encrypted. Avo Hub switches by itself.
how.demoLabel: A walk-through of pairing. Nothing on this page connects to anything.
how.addInstalling: Putting Avo Hub on the phone
how.codeText: Your phone shows a code too. Pair only if both codes are the same.
how.codeCompare: Compare with the code on Pixel 9.
how.routeCableText: USB · 4 ms. Full control: tap and type from the Mac.
how.routeWifiText: Over your home network. The cable can go back in the drawer.
how.routeNetText: From anywhere, end-to-end encrypted. Your phone still decides what this Mac may do.
how.readiness: Many phone brands add battery savers and settings that get in the way. The readiness check on the phone finds each one and shows you what to do.
how.privacy: Your phone decides what each Mac may do, feature by feature, and keeps a record of it. An account is optional, and over the internet everything travels encrypted.

pricing.title: Free over a cable and Wi‑Fi.
pricing.lede: Pay only to use it over the internet without limits, and for a few extras.
pricing.freeText: The phone's screen, notifications, messages, contacts, gallery, files and webcam over a cable and the same Wi‑Fi, for as many phones as you like. A free account adds 1 GB of internet use per device each month; notifications and messages don't count.
pricing.proPer: a month for the first device
pricing.proExtra: $1 a month for each one after, or $20 and $10 a year.
pricing.pro1: No monthly internet allowance, within fair use
pricing.pro2: Full quality over the internet and on the web
pricing.pro3: Your phone's camera as a webcam over the internet
pricing.pro4: Several extra displays at once, up to 120 Hz
pricing.note: Prices are in US dollars; taxes are added at checkout where they apply. Payments are handled by Paddle.

req.phoneText: Or a tablet, on Android 11 or newer.
req.cableTitle: A USB cable that carries data

avo.title: Made to go with Avo.
avo.text: Avo runs Android apps and games on your Mac with no phone at all; Avo Hub connects the one you own. They're separate apps: use one, or both. A game you set up in Avo starts with the same key layout in Avo Hub.
avo.openText: Open source like Avo, under the same Apache 2.0 license, with all the code on GitHub.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Yes, over a cable and the same Wi‑Fi, with or without an account. Pro adds internet use without a monthly allowance and a few extras, from $2 a month. See pricing.
faq.a2: No. Without one, you pair each phone with a QR code and six digits. With one, the phones, Macs and browsers on your account connect without pairing each one.
faq.a3: Any brand with Android 11 or newer, phones and tablets. Some brands add battery savers that get in the way; the readiness check on the phone finds them and shows what to do.
faq.q4: Does it work when I'm away from home?
faq.a4: Yes, over the internet, end-to-end encrypted. At home it uses the cable or the same Wi‑Fi, and it switches by itself.
faq.q5: Can I use it from a browser?
faq.a5: Yes. With an account, Avo Hub Web reaches your phones and Avo Remote Web reaches your Mac, in any modern browser.
faq.q6: Does it work with an iPhone?
faq.a6: No. Avo Hub is for Android phones and tablets.
faq.q7: Why do some apps show black?
faq.a7: Apps that protect their screen, such as some banking and streaming apps, show black in the window. That's Android keeping them private.
faq.a8: Avo Hub is in development. The first preview will be a disk image for your Mac; Avo Hub then puts its app on your phone over USB.
